newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Genting 96 net up 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Genting 96 net up 4 pct.

text.p: Gaming and hotels firm Genting Bhd said on Tuesday its 1996 net earnings rose four percent to 571.29 million ringgit ($230.4 million), matching market forecasts.
It reported net earnings of 551.76 million ringgit for the previous year ended December 31, 1995.
Genting, which operates Malaysia's sole casino through its 54 percent-owned Resorts World Bhd, said in a statement that 1996 turnover also rose four percent to 2.60 billion ringgit.
The mountain-top casino is located just outside Malaysia's capital Kuala Lumpur, where Resorts World also operates hotels and theme parks.
Genting, controlled by tycoon Lim Goh Tong and his family, also has holdings in plantations, properties and power generation.
The company's pretax profit was up seven percent to 1.19 billion ringgit and earnings per share was 81.4 Malaysian cents against 78.6 cents the previous year.
Equity analysts who follow the stock had on average forecast Genting's net earnings at 577.4 million ringgit.
Analysts have said the company's main revenue producers -- the casino and hotels -- were hampered by ongoing renovations and by competition from overseas venues.

Resorts World also reported a four percent rise in its net earnings to 569.73 million ringgit. Turnover rose 13 percent to 2.11 billion and pretax profit by nine percent to 802.9 million ringgit. ($1=2.4800 ringgit)
